Single-cell RNA-seq analyses usually sort cells into clusters and give each
cluster one label. Many questions, though, are about **cells in transition**:
cells that are differentiating, maturing or responding to a stimulus. This
3-hour workshop treats such cell states as **continuous**, using snRNA-seq of
the maturing human heart.

## Data

snRNA-seq of the human heart at foetal, young and adult stages:

> Sim CB, et al. Sex-specific control of human heart maturation by the
> progesterone receptor. *Circulation* 2021;143(16):1614–1628.
> [doi:10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.120.051921](https://doi.org/10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.120.051921)

The Φ-Space reference is a subset of the Gao et al. (2026, *Genome Biology*)
snRNA-seq atlas of the human left ventricle.

## Running the materials yourself

The pages on this site were rendered from the workshop's saved results. To
run the code, you need R 4.6 (Bioconductor 3.23), the
[workshop repository](https://github.com/mao-lab-org/scWorkshop) and its data.
From the repository root:

```r
source("setup/install_packages.R")   # R packages
source("setup/download_data.R")      # data + saved results from Zenodo (~2.7 GB)
source("setup/check_setup.R")        # verify
```

Then open the files in `vignettes/` in RStudio and run the chunks in order.
